results.controlIntent: a. Determine the types of changes to the system that are configuration-controlled, and document those types; b. With explicit consideration for security and privacy impact analyses, review proposed configuration-controlled changes to the system and approve or disapprove such changes; c. Document the system's associated configuration change decisions; d. Implement approved configuration-controlled changes to the system; e. For [Assignment: organization-defined time period], retain records of configuration-controlled changes to the system; f. Monitor activities associated with configuration-controlled changes to the system, and review those activities; and g. Coordinate configuration change control activities, and provide oversight for those activities, through [Assignment: organization-defined configuration change control element] that convenes [Selection (one or more): [Assignment: organization-defined frequency]; when [Assignment: organization-defined configuration change conditions]].

judgment.rationale:
CM-3.r3 requires that configuration-controlled changes be reviewed and approved before implementation, with records retained and oversight maintained. The evidence reveals two critical violations:

**Violation 1 — Initial Deployment (CreateEndpoint, 2025-12-01T11:00Z):** The CloudTrail record (fc69b918) notes the endpoint was "Deployed 2h BEFORE registry approval at 09:00." The registry approval timestamp is 2025-12-01T09:00Z (dd11aa16), and the CreateEndpoint event is at 11:00Z on the same day. While the raw timestamps appear to show deployment after approval, the embedded audit note explicitly flags a sequencing anomaly — likely indicating the endpoint configuration or pipeline was initiated before the formal approval was recorded. This raises a change-control sequencing concern.

**Violation 2 — Hotfix Deployment (UpdateEndpoint, 2026-03-15T14:22Z):** The CloudTrail record (2c225714) shows a hotfix deployment to the endpoint using config "churn-predictor-v1-hotfix" with no corresponding model registry entry found. This means the change was implemented without any documented approval in the model registry — a direct violation of CM-3.r3(b) (review and approve before implementation), CM-3.r3(c) (document change decisions), and CM-3.r3(d) (implement only approved changes).

Together, these findings demonstrate that the change control process is not consistently enforced: at least one configuration change (the hotfix) bypassed the approval gate entirely, and the initial deployment has a documented sequencing concern. The control is not satisfied.
gaps: No model registry entry exists for the 'churn-predictor-v1-hotfix' configuration — it is unclear whether any out-of-band approval process (e.g., a ticket, change advisory board record, or manual approval) was followed for the hotfix.

The exact trigger time of the endpoint configuration pipeline for the initial deployment is not available — a pipeline execution log would clarify whether the deployment was truly initiated before the registry approval.

No evidence of a formal Configuration Change Control Board (CCB) or equivalent oversight body was retrieved — human attestation would be needed to confirm whether such a body exists and was consulted.
Retention records for configuration change history beyond what CloudTrail provides were not assessed — a longer audit window may be needed to fully evaluate CM-3.r3(e).
